# Adjudication Task — Chapter 451

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃451화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|“은인, 어디 가세요?”
  6|
  7|“으, 응?”
  8|
  9|문밖으로 슬그머니 걸음을 옮기던 나는 움찔했다. 주섬주섬 짐을 챙긴 청풍이 고개를 갸웃거리며 나를 바라보고 있었다.
 10|
 11|“뭐가, 왜.”
 12|
 13|“어디 가시는 거 아니에요?”
 14|
 15|“그, 잠깐 급한 볼일이 생겨서.”
 16|
 17|“빨리 출발해야 한다고 하셨잖아요?”
 18|
 19|“이봐, 청 소협. 내가 굳이 이런 말까지는 안 하려고 했는데…….”
 20|
 21|나는 짐짓 얼굴을 굳히며 입을 열었다.
 22|
 23|“소피보러 가는 거야. 됐지?”
 24|
 25|“하지만 측간은 그 방향이 아닌데요.”
 26|
 27|“…….”
 28|
 29|쓸데없이 예리하네.
 30|
 31|부전공은 무공이고, 전공이 먹고 싸는 일이라 그런지 섬 안의 측간은 죄다 알고 있는 것이 틀림없다.
 32|
 33|잠시 머뭇거리던 내가 대답했다.
 34|
 35|“……노상 방뇨야.”
 36|
 37|내가 생각하기에도 궁색한 변명이다.
 38|
 39|그제야 이상함을 느낀 궁기방과 혁무진도 행낭을 꾸리다 말고 이쪽으로 고개를 틀었다.
 40|
 41|“궁 소협. 조장님께서 오늘따라 혓바닥이 좀 기신 것 같지 않아요?”
 42|
 43|“그러게. 왜 저렇게 안절부절못하는 것 같지?”
 44|
 45|“그건 너희 둘 중에 누구부터 때릴까 고민돼서 그래.”
 46|
 47|평소 같았다면 이 말을 던진 시점에서 꼬리를 내려야 하는데, 이미 내 폭력에 길들여진 두 놈은 제법 성장해 있었다.
 48|
 49|“흠. 평소의 조장님이었다면 이미 말보다 손이 먼저 나왔을 겁니다. 그런데 말로 얼버무린다? 확실히 뭔가 있어요.”
 50|
 51|“그렇지?”
 52|
 53|“확실합니다. 제가 그동안 한두 번 맞아 본 줄 아세요? 이게 다 개연성과 흐름이 있어요.”
 54|
 55|혁무진이 게슴츠레한 눈빛으로 나를 바라보던 그때, 눈을 번쩍 뜬 궁기방이 주위를 훑었다.
 56|
 57|“잠깐, 그런데 문경이는 어디 갔어?”
 58|
 59|“어, 그러게요. 조금 전까지만 해도 같이 있었는데, 이 녀석 도대체 어딜 간 거지?”
 60|
 61|어딜 가긴. 이미 밖으로 나가서 날 기다리고 있지.
 62|
 63|
 64|
 65|‘얘기 좀 하지.’
 66|
 67|
 68|
 69|나는 조금 전 문경이 흘리고 간 전음을 떠올리며 한숨을 내쉬었다.
 70|
 71|여기서 더 부정했다가는 괜한 의심만 더 받게 생겼다.
 72|
 73|“밖에 있어. 나랑 따로 나눌 이야기가 있어서.”
 74|
 75|“측간에서요? 그것도 단둘이?”
 76|
 77|“……뭔 개소리야, 미친놈아. 그렇게 말하니까 의미심장하게 들리잖아.”
 78|
 79|혁무진이 의뭉스러운 표정으로 나를 바라보며 말했다.
 80|
 81|“조장님. 전 이미 욕과 폭력에 길들어진 놈이라 괜찮습니다. 하지만 문경이한테는 이상한 물 들게 하지 마십쇼.”
 82|
 83|“…….”
 84|
 85|미친놈이 뭐라는 거야. 당장 내가 피로 물들게 생겼구만.
 86|
 87|하도 어이가 없어서 말도 제대로 못 하는 내게, 궁기방이 한마디를 보탰다.
 88|
 89|“혁가놈 말이 맞다. 애가 볼수록 참 생각이 깊고 착하던데, 괜한 트집 잡아서 괴롭히지 말아라.”
 90|
 91|“와, 이 새끼들 진짜…… 아니다. 됐다. 너희가 뭘 알겠냐.”
 92|
 93|그나마 이제야 상황을 눈치챈 청풍은 꿀 먹은 벙어리처럼 입을 다물고…… 아니, 지금 보니까 진짜 당과 처먹고 있네.
 94|
 95|‘저놈의 당과는 도대체 어디서 계속 튀어나오는 거야.’
 96|
 97|더 있다가는 정신병 걸리겠다.
 98|
 99|고개를 절레절레 흔든 나는 뒤에서 들려오는 목소리를 무시하고 가옥을 나섰다.
100|
101|밖으로 나오자, 새하얀 백의를 걸친 문경이 마당에서 나를 기다리고 있었다.
102|
103|“늦으셨군요.”
104|
105|“그래도 얼마 안 걸렸…….”
106|
107|“늦으셨군요.”
108|
109|“미안하…….”
110|
111|“늦으셨군요.”
112|
113|“…….”
114|
115|제발 살려 줘.
116|
117|반복재생의 압박이 장난 아니다. 누구도 눈치 못 챌 만큼 은밀하게 쏘아지는 기세에 나는 마른침을 꿀꺽 삼켰다.
118|
119|“느, 늦어서 미안하다. 그런데 무슨 일이야?”
120|
121|“네?”
122|
123|“응?”
124|
125|“그게 무슨 말씀이십니까. 아까 공자님께서 제게 할 말이 있다고 불러내셨으면서.”
126|
127|칸 영화제가 선정한 올해의 배우인가.
128|
129|정말 아무것도 모른다는 듯이 눈을 깜빡이는 모습에 순간 나까지 속아 넘어갔을 정도다.
130|
131|소년 의생의 껍질을 뒤집어쓴 괴물이 맑게 웃으며 말을 이었다.
132|
133|“아, 잠깐 자리를 옮기자고요? 알겠습니다.”
134|
135|“아냐. 될 수 있으면 그냥 이 자리에서 얘기하는 게 좋을 것 같…….”
136|
137|“아, 잠깐 자리를 옮기자고요? 알겠습니다.”
138|
139|“……그래, 그러자.”
140|
141|엄마 보고 싶다.
142|
143|나는 눈물을 머금고 문경을 따라 걷기 시작했다.
144|
145|드문드문 보이는 제갈세가와 무당파, 수룡채 수적들을 피해 인적이 끊긴 곳으로 접어들자 비로소 문경의 입이 열렸다.
146|
147|“암천(暗天). 놈들의 소행이냐?”
148|
149|“어, 아무래도 그런 것 같은데.”
150|
151|“여기 사람 없다.”
152|
153|나는 빛의 속도로 말을 정정했다.
154|
155|“그런 것 같습니다.”
156|
157|“아직 확실하지는 않은 모양이로군.”
158|
159|“언제나 일말의 가능성은 있으니까요. 하지만 진법이 발견되지 않았을 뿐, 암천의 소행이 확실하다고 봅니다.”
160|
161|“암천이라, 암천…….”
162|
163|낮게 뇌까린 문경이 문득 고개를 들었다.
164|
165|보름달마저 모습을 감춘 어두운 밤하늘을 말없이 응시하던 그는 잠시 후 불쑥 입을 열었다.
166|
167|“시신들을 보며 이상한 점을 느끼지 못했느냐?”
168|
169|“이상한 점이라면……?”
170|
171|“시신에 남겨진 상흔(傷痕).”
172|
173|모든 죽음은 흔적을 남긴다. 특히 무림인들 간의 싸움에서 발생한 사망이라면 더더욱 그렇다.
174|
175|견문이 넓고 여러 무공의 특징에 대해 꿰뚫고 있는 고수라면 시신에 남은 상흔만으로도 어떤 병장기를 사용했는지, 어떤 초식으로 망자를 죽음에 이르게 했는지 단번에 파악할 수도 있다고 들었다.
176|
177|그리고 지금 내 눈앞에 있는 이 소년 의생은 그럴 만한 안목과 무공을 갖춘, 무림 최고의 검시관 중 하나다.
178|
179|“처음 보는 상흔이었다. 아주 기본적인 삼재검법(三才劍法)의 무리를 따른 것 같으면서도, 파도처럼 출렁이는. 아주 희한하고 묘한 상흔이야.”
180|
181|문경이 천천히 손을 들어 허공을 향해 휘저었다. 올올이 흘러나온 공력이 어둠 속에서 희미한 빛을 뿜어낸다.
182|
183|“유추해 보건대, 흉수가 사용한 것은 흔히 찾아볼 수 있는 병장기가 아니다. 검신이 구불구불한 사검(蛇劍)에 가까운 기병이야.”
184|
185|“저는 강기(罡氣)로 베었다고 생각했습니다.”
186|
187|“네 짐작이 맞다. 강기, 혹은 강기 만큼이나 예리한 무언가가 분명해.”
188|
189|강기만큼이나 예리한 무언가라면 만년한철이 유일하다.
190|
191|그리고 암천이 아무리 준비를 철저히 했다 하여도 그 많은 병력들이 만년한철로 만든 병장기를 사용할 리는 없었다.
192|
193|‘황금이 아무리 많아도 구하기 힘든 것이 만년한철이니까.’
194|
195|이건 자본이 아니라 자원 희소성의 문제다. 잠시 생각에 잠겨 있던 내게 문경이 물었다.
196|
197|“시신을 모두 살펴보았느냐?”
198|
199|“전부는 아니고, 눈에 띄는 시신들은 봤습니다. 제가 그리 견문이 넓은 편이 아니라서, 직접 봐도 무슨 무공과 초식인지 잘 모르겠더군요.”
200|
201|“네가 본 시신 중에는 장강일도 황충의 것도 있었다. 어땠느냐?”
202|
203|“강기에 의해 단숨에 허리가 끊겼습니다. 다만 부패가 너무 심한 나머지 거기까지밖에는…….”
204|
205|“하면 광수도귀와 파랑호는?”
206|
207|“그건…….”
208|
209|나는 문득 눈살을 찌푸렸다. 갑자기 세 구의 시신이 가진 공통점이 떠올랐기 때문이었다.
210|
211|‘……상반신만 남아 있었어.’
212|
213|세 구의 시신 모두, 떨어져 나간 하반신은 어디에서도 찾을 수 없었다.
214|
215|앞서 그런 시신 여러 구를 본 탓에 당시로서는 이상함을 느끼지 못했는데, 확실히 의문이 드는 부분이다.
216|
217|“물고기들이 뜯어 먹은 게 아니었습니까?”
218|
219|“그것도 틀린 말은 아니겠지. 살펴본 바에 의하면 동정채의 몰살은 이미 열흘 전의 일이다. 추위가 사라진 지 오래이니 부패가 심한 것은 당연하며, 물에 잠긴 시신들은 말할 것도 없을 것이다.”
220|
221|따사로운 햇볕과 축축한 습기는 죽음이 남긴 많은 흔적을 지워 버렸다.
222|
223|하지만 그것과는 별개로, 또 다른 흔적까지 지우지는 못했다.
224|
225|“그에 비해 양민들의 시신은 비교적 사지가 온전했다. 이 사실을 알고 있었느냐?”
226|
227|“예. 무공을 익히지 않은 이들의 경우에는 보통 베인 것이 아니라 으스러졌더군요.”
228|
229|어린아이와 여인, 노약자들은 다른 수적들의 시신과 달리 몸뚱어리가 절단되지는 않았다. 다만 전신이 으스러지고, 뭉개졌을 뿐이다.
230|
231|그리고 거기에 한 가지 더.
232|
233|“가옥과 주위의 지면이 온통 무너져 있더군. 이는 만근의 힘이 가해지지 않고서야 불가능한 일이며, 고강한 공력을 지닌 내가고수가 택할 만한 수법이 아니다.”
234|
235|“그러니까, 외공(外功)의 고수다?”
236|
237|“여기 사람 없다니까.”
238|
239|“……그냥 혼잣말이었습니다.”
240|
241|거, 되게 예민하게 구네.
242|
243|황급히 변명한 나는 잠깐 생각에 잠겼다.
244|
245|무림에서의 무공은 크게 두 분류로 나뉜다. 공력의 효율과 활용을 중시하는 내공. 그리고 공력을 사용하기는 하나, 신체를 극한으로 단련하는 외공.
246|
247|무공에 입문함과 동시에 두 가지 선택지를 마주한 사람들은 대부분 전자를 택한다.
248|
249|외공 수련이 매우 고통스럽다는 이유도 있지만, 성과를 이루기 위해서는 기나긴 인고의 시간이 필요하기 때문이었다.
250|
251|‘그건 즉, 이 정도 파괴력을 낼 수 있는 초절정의 외공 고수가 손에 꼽는다는 뜻이지.’
252|
253|애초에 천하를 거꾸로 뒤집어 탈탈 털어 봐도 얼마 없는 초절정 고수다.
254|
255|답을 구하는 눈빛으로 슬쩍 문경을 바라보자, 소년 의생의 매끈한 이마에 작은 주름이 잡혔다.
256|
257|“그렇게 봐도 소용없다. 나 역시 놈의 정체를 모르니. 아니, 놈이 아니라 놈들이라고 해야겠군.”
258|
259|“두 명입니까?”
260|
261|“적어도 둘. 많으면 셋이다.”
262|
263|“초절정 고수가 셋이나…….”
264|
265|“짐작하기로는 사천에서 상대했던 기련삼괴 이상이다. 적어도 그중 하나는 특이한 기병을 사용하는 자고.”
266|
267|아니, 시벌. 별이 다섯 개도 아니고 무슨 초절정 고수가 셋씩이나 있냐.
268|
269|문경과 적천강이 떡 버티고 있으니 망정이지, 그렇지 않았다면 무슨 일이 생길까 봐 자리도 못 비웠을 거다.
270|
271|“이 정도 정보면 삼괴(三怪), 그놈이 알 수도 있겠네요. 그래도 한솥밥 먹는 동료들이 누군지는 들어 봤을 테니까요.”
272|
273|사천에서 생포한 삼괴는 내가 제갈세가로 가는 이유 중 하나다.
274|
275|불알이 으스러진 이후로 조울증 환자처럼 변했다고 들었는데, 성심성의껏 조진다면 얼마 버티지 못할 것이다.
276|
277|‘어쩌면 놈을 앞세워서 진법을 찾아낼 수도 있고.’
278|
279|희망찬 생각에 잠겨 있던 바로 그 순간이었다.
280|
281|“어쩌면 이미 모두가 알고 있는 사람인지도 모른다.”
282|
283|“예?”
284|
285|“기병을 쓰는 그놈 말이다.”
286|
287|그 말의 뜻을 이해하는 데에는 제법 오랜 시간이 필요했다. 망치로 뒤통수를 한 대 얻어맞은 듯한 충격.
288|

[P121]

[P122]

[P123]
Martial arts in Murim could broadly be divided into two categories.

[P124]
Internal arts emphasized the efficient use and application of internal energy. External arts also used internal energy, but focused on tempering the body to its absolute limits.

[P125]
Most people faced those two paths upon entering the world of martial arts, and most chose the former.

[P126]
Partly because training in external arts was excruciating, but also because achieving any meaningful results required long years of grueling perseverance.

[P127]
*Which means there are only a handful of Supreme Peak external-arts masters capable of this level of destruction.*

[P128]
There were hardly any Supreme Peak masters in the world to begin with, even if you turned the whole realm upside down and shook it out.

[P129]
I glanced at Mungyeong, silently asking for an answer. A faint crease appeared on the young medical apprentice’s smooth forehead.

[P130]
“Looking at me will do you no good. I do not know his identity either. No—I should say their identities, not his.”

[P131]
“There are two?”

[P132]
“At least two. Three at most.”

[P133]
“Three Supreme Peak masters…”

[P134]
“I would estimate that they are at least as formidable as the Qilian Three Fiends we faced in Sichuan. And at least one of them uses an unusual weapon.”

[P135]
*Fuck. What was this, some five-star rating? Why the hell were there three Supreme Peak masters together?*

[P136]

[P137]
“With this much information, the Third Fiend might know something. He must have at least heard who his comrades were.”

[P138]
The Third Fiend we had captured in Sichuan was one of the reasons I was going to the Zhuge Clan.

[P139]
I had heard that he had become like a bipolar patient after his balls were crushed, but if I worked him over with enough care and dedication, he would not last long.

[P140]
*Maybe we can even put him out front and have him lead us to the formation.*

[P141]
That hopeful thought had barely crossed my mind when Mungyeong spoke.

[P142]
“Perhaps it is someone everyone already knows.”

[P143]
“What?”

[P144]
“I mean the one who uses that unusual weapon.”

[P145]

[P146]
The realization struck like a hammer to the back of my head.

[P147]
I stared blankly at Mungyeong.

[P148]
“Are you serious?”

[P149]
“A seasoned Supreme Peak master. Forms and wounds so unusual that they are difficult to read. There cannot be many people at that realm who wield such a weapon.”

[P150]
“Then it really is…”

[P151]
A dry voice emerged from between Mungyeong’s lips.

[P152]
“The Dongting Fisherman. For now, he is the most likely suspect.”

[P153]
“…!”

[P154]
The eccentric master who had never left the area around Dongting Lake in his entire life.

[P155]
A Supreme Peak master who, unusually, used a fishing rod made of black wood as his signature weapon. Enraged by the tragic news concerning his friend, the head of the Sea Serpent Society, he had crossed Tianling Falls and disappeared.

[P156]
*Everything fits perfectly.*

[P157]
I had forgotten about him for a moment.

[P158]
This was no baseless suspicion.

[P159]
Unlike the others, the Dongting Fisherman’s corpse had never been found. The only trace he had left behind was his broken black-wood fishing rod.

[P160]
It was only a guess, but what if the Dongting Fisherman really was a member of Dark Heaven?

[P161]
“But the Dongting Fisherman Great Hero Zhuge told me about had no reason to do anything like this…”

[P162]

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 451

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃451화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|“은인, 어디 가세요?”
  6|
  7|“으, 응?”
  8|
  9|문밖으로 슬그머니 걸음을 옮기던 나는 움찔했다. 주섬주섬 짐을 챙긴 청풍이 고개를 갸웃거리며 나를 바라보고 있었다.
 10|
 11|“뭐가, 왜.”
 12|
 13|“어디 가시는 거 아니에요?”
 14|
 15|“그, 잠깐 급한 볼일이 생겨서.”
 16|
 17|“빨리 출발해야 한다고 하셨잖아요?”
 18|
 19|“이봐, 청 소협. 내가 굳이 이런 말까지는 안 하려고 했는데…….”
 20|
 21|나는 짐짓 얼굴을 굳히며 입을 열었다.
 22|
 23|“소피보러 가는 거야. 됐지?”
 24|
 25|“하지만 측간은 그 방향이 아닌데요.”
 26|
 27|“…….”
 28|
 29|쓸데없이 예리하네.
 30|
 31|부전공은 무공이고, 전공이 먹고 싸는 일이라 그런지 섬 안의 측간은 죄다 알고 있는 것이 틀림없다.
 32|
 33|잠시 머뭇거리던 내가 대답했다.
 34|
 35|“……노상 방뇨야.”
 36|
 37|내가 생각하기에도 궁색한 변명이다.
 38|
 39|그제야 이상함을 느낀 궁기방과 혁무진도 행낭을 꾸리다 말고 이쪽으로 고개를 틀었다.
 40|
 41|“궁 소협. 조장님께서 오늘따라 혓바닥이 좀 기신 것 같지 않아요?”
 42|
 43|“그러게. 왜 저렇게 안절부절못하는 것 같지?”
 44|
 45|“그건 너희 둘 중에 누구부터 때릴까 고민돼서 그래.”
 46|
 47|평소 같았다면 이 말을 던진 시점에서 꼬리를 내려야 하는데, 이미 내 폭력에 길들여진 두 놈은 제법 성장해 있었다.
 48|
 49|“흠. 평소의 조장님이었다면 이미 말보다 손이 먼저 나왔을 겁니다. 그런데 말로 얼버무린다? 확실히 뭔가 있어요.”
 50|
 51|“그렇지?”
 52|
 53|“확실합니다. 제가 그동안 한두 번 맞아 본 줄 아세요? 이게 다 개연성과 흐름이 있어요.”
 54|
 55|혁무진이 게슴츠레한 눈빛으로 나를 바라보던 그때, 눈을 번쩍 뜬 궁기방이 주위를 훑었다.
 56|
 57|“잠깐, 그런데 문경이는 어디 갔어?”
 58|
 59|“어, 그러게요. 조금 전까지만 해도 같이 있었는데, 이 녀석 도대체 어딜 간 거지?”
 60|
 61|어딜 가긴. 이미 밖으로 나가서 날 기다리고 있지.
 62|
 63|
 64|
 65|‘얘기 좀 하지.’
 66|
 67|
 68|
 69|나는 조금 전 문경이 흘리고 간 전음을 떠올리며 한숨을 내쉬었다.
 70|
 71|여기서 더 부정했다가는 괜한 의심만 더 받게 생겼다.
 72|
 73|“밖에 있어. 나랑 따로 나눌 이야기가 있어서.”
 74|
 75|“측간에서요? 그것도 단둘이?”
 76|
 77|“……뭔 개소리야, 미친놈아. 그렇게 말하니까 의미심장하게 들리잖아.”
 78|
 79|혁무진이 의뭉스러운 표정으로 나를 바라보며 말했다.
 80|
 81|“조장님. 전 이미 욕과 폭력에 길들어진 놈이라 괜찮습니다. 하지만 문경이한테는 이상한 물 들게 하지 마십쇼.”
 82|
 83|“…….”
 84|
 85|미친놈이 뭐라는 거야. 당장 내가 피로 물들게 생겼구만.
 86|
 87|하도 어이가 없어서 말도 제대로 못 하는 내게, 궁기방이 한마디를 보탰다.
 88|
 89|“혁가놈 말이 맞다. 애가 볼수록 참 생각이 깊고 착하던데, 괜한 트집 잡아서 괴롭히지 말아라.”
 90|
 91|“와, 이 새끼들 진짜…… 아니다. 됐다. 너희가 뭘 알겠냐.”
 92|
 93|그나마 이제야 상황을 눈치챈 청풍은 꿀 먹은 벙어리처럼 입을 다물고…… 아니, 지금 보니까 진짜 당과 처먹고 있네.
 94|
 95|‘저놈의 당과는 도대체 어디서 계속 튀어나오는 거야.’
 96|
 97|더 있다가는 정신병 걸리겠다.
 98|
 99|고개를 절레절레 흔든 나는 뒤에서 들려오는 목소리를 무시하고 가옥을 나섰다.
100|
101|밖으로 나오자, 새하얀 백의를 걸친 문경이 마당에서 나를 기다리고 있었다.
102|
103|“늦으셨군요.”
104|
105|“그래도 얼마 안 걸렸…….”
106|
107|“늦으셨군요.”
108|
109|“미안하…….”
110|
111|“늦으셨군요.”
112|
113|“…….”
114|
115|제발 살려 줘.
116|
117|반복재생의 압박이 장난 아니다. 누구도 눈치 못 챌 만큼 은밀하게 쏘아지는 기세에 나는 마른침을 꿀꺽 삼켰다.
118|
119|“느, 늦어서 미안하다. 그런데 무슨 일이야?”
120|
121|“네?”
122|
123|“응?”
124|
125|“그게 무슨 말씀이십니까. 아까 공자님께서 제게 할 말이 있다고 불러내셨으면서.”
126|
127|칸 영화제가 선정한 올해의 배우인가.
128|
129|정말 아무것도 모른다는 듯이 눈을 깜빡이는 모습에 순간 나까지 속아 넘어갔을 정도다.
130|
131|소년 의생의 껍질을 뒤집어쓴 괴물이 맑게 웃으며 말을 이었다.
132|
133|“아, 잠깐 자리를 옮기자고요? 알겠습니다.”
134|
135|“아냐. 될 수 있으면 그냥 이 자리에서 얘기하는 게 좋을 것 같…….”
136|
137|“아, 잠깐 자리를 옮기자고요? 알겠습니다.”
138|
139|“……그래, 그러자.”
140|
141|엄마 보고 싶다.
142|
143|나는 눈물을 머금고 문경을 따라 걷기 시작했다.
144|
145|드문드문 보이는 제갈세가와 무당파, 수룡채 수적들을 피해 인적이 끊긴 곳으로 접어들자 비로소 문경의 입이 열렸다.
146|
147|“암천(暗天). 놈들의 소행이냐?”
148|
149|“어, 아무래도 그런 것 같은데.”
150|
151|“여기 사람 없다.”
152|
153|나는 빛의 속도로 말을 정정했다.
154|
155|“그런 것 같습니다.”
156|
157|“아직 확실하지는 않은 모양이로군.”
158|
159|“언제나 일말의 가능성은 있으니까요. 하지만 진법이 발견되지 않았을 뿐, 암천의 소행이 확실하다고 봅니다.”
160|
161|“암천이라, 암천…….”
162|
163|낮게 뇌까린 문경이 문득 고개를 들었다.
164|
165|보름달마저 모습을 감춘 어두운 밤하늘을 말없이 응시하던 그는 잠시 후 불쑥 입을 열었다.
166|
167|“시신들을 보며 이상한 점을 느끼지 못했느냐?”
168|
169|“이상한 점이라면……?”
170|
171|“시신에 남겨진 상흔(傷痕).”
172|
173|모든 죽음은 흔적을 남긴다. 특히 무림인들 간의 싸움에서 발생한 사망이라면 더더욱 그렇다.
174|
175|견문이 넓고 여러 무공의 특징에 대해 꿰뚫고 있는 고수라면 시신에 남은 상흔만으로도 어떤 병장기를 사용했는지, 어떤 초식으로 망자를 죽음에 이르게 했는지 단번에 파악할 수도 있다고 들었다.
176|
177|그리고 지금 내 눈앞에 있는 이 소년 의생은 그럴 만한 안목과 무공을 갖춘, 무림 최고의 검시관 중 하나다.
178|
179|“처음 보는 상흔이었다. 아주 기본적인 삼재검법(三才劍法)의 무리를 따른 것 같으면서도, 파도처럼 출렁이는. 아주 희한하고 묘한 상흔이야.”
180|
181|문경이 천천히 손을 들어 허공을 향해 휘저었다. 올올이 흘러나온 공력이 어둠 속에서 희미한 빛을 뿜어낸다.
182|
183|“유추해 보건대, 흉수가 사용한 것은 흔히 찾아볼 수 있는 병장기가 아니다. 검신이 구불구불한 사검(蛇劍)에 가까운 기병이야.”
184|
185|“저는 강기(罡氣)로 베었다고 생각했습니다.”
186|
187|“네 짐작이 맞다. 강기, 혹은 강기 만큼이나 예리한 무언가가 분명해.”
188|
189|강기만큼이나 예리한 무언가라면 만년한철이 유일하다.
190|
191|그리고 암천이 아무리 준비를 철저히 했다 하여도 그 많은 병력들이 만년한철로 만든 병장기를 사용할 리는 없었다.
192|
193|‘황금이 아무리 많아도 구하기 힘든 것이 만년한철이니까.’
194|
195|이건 자본이 아니라 자원 희소성의 문제다. 잠시 생각에 잠겨 있던 내게 문경이 물었다.
196|
197|“시신을 모두 살펴보았느냐?”
198|
199|“전부는 아니고, 눈에 띄는 시신들은 봤습니다. 제가 그리 견문이 넓은 편이 아니라서, 직접 봐도 무슨 무공과 초식인지 잘 모르겠더군요.”
200|
201|“네가 본 시신 중에는 장강일도 황충의 것도 있었다. 어땠느냐?”
202|
203|“강기에 의해 단숨에 허리가 끊겼습니다. 다만 부패가 너무 심한 나머지 거기까지밖에는…….”
204|
205|“하면 광수도귀와 파랑호는?”
206|
207|“그건…….”
208|
209|나는 문득 눈살을 찌푸렸다. 갑자기 세 구의 시신이 가진 공통점이 떠올랐기 때문이었다.
210|
211|‘……상반신만 남아 있었어.’
212|
213|세 구의 시신 모두, 떨어져 나간 하반신은 어디에서도 찾을 수 없었다.
214|
215|앞서 그런 시신 여러 구를 본 탓에 당시로서는 이상함을 느끼지 못했는데, 확실히 의문이 드는 부분이다.
216|

[P26]
“Absolutely. Do you think I’ve only been beaten once or twice? There’s a logic and flow to these things.”

[P27]

[P28]
“Wait. Where did Mungyeong go?”

[P29]
“Oh, you’re right. He was here a moment ago. Where the hell did he go?”

[P30]

[P31]
*Let’s talk.*

[P32]

[P33]
Denying it any longer would only make them more suspicious.

[P34]
“He’s outside. We have something to discuss in private.”

[P35]
“In the privy? Just the two of you?”

[P36]
“…What the hell are you talking about, you lunatic? You’re making it sound suggestive.”

[P37]
Hyuk Mujin gave me a dubious look.

[P38]
“Captain, I’ve already been conditioned to insults and violence, so I’ll be fine. But please don’t expose Mungyeong to any strange influences.”

[P39]
“…”

[P40]

[P41]
I was too dumbfounded to speak, and Gung Gibang added his two cents.

[P42]
“Hyuk’s right. The more I see that kid, the more thoughtful and kind he seems. Don’t pick on him for no reason.”

[P43]
“Wow. You bastards, seriously…”

[P44]
I stopped myself.

[P45]
“Forget it. What would you two know?”

[P46]
Cheongpung had at least finally caught on and fallen silent as if he’d swallowed honey…

[P47]
No, now that I looked closer, he really was stuffing candy into his mouth.

[P48]
*Where does he keep getting that candy?*

[P49]
If I stayed here any longer, I was going to lose my mind.

[P50]
Shaking my head, I ignored the voices behind me and left the house.

[P51]
Outside, Mungyeong stood waiting in the courtyard, dressed in spotless white robes.

[P52]
“You’re late.”

[P53]
“It didn’t take that long…”

[P54]
“You’re late.”

[P55]
“Sorry…”

[P56]
“You’re late.”

[P57]
“…”

[P58]
*Please save me.*

[P59]
The pressure of that broken-record routine was no joke. His aura bore down on me so subtly that no one else could detect it, and I swallowed hard.

[P60]
“S-sorry I’m late. But what’s going on?”

[P61]
“Pardon?”

[P62]
“Huh?”

[P63]
“What do you mean? You called me out earlier because you had something to say.”

[P64]
Had Cannes named him Actor of the Year or something?

[P65]
He blinked as if he truly had no idea what I was talking about. For a moment, even I nearly fell for it.

[P66]
The monster wearing the skin of a young medical apprentice smiled brightly and continued.

[P67]
“Oh, you want us to move somewhere else for a moment? Understood.”

[P68]
“No. If possible, I think it would be better to talk right here…”

[P69]
“Oh, you want us to move somewhere else for a moment? Understood.”

[P70]
“…Fine. Let’s go.”

[P71]
I miss my mother.

[P72]
Holding back tears, I followed Mungyeong.

[P73]
We avoided the occasional disciples of the Zhuge Clan and Wudang, along with the river bandits of Water Dragon Stronghold, until we reached a deserted area. Only then did Mungyeong finally speak.

[P74]
“Dark Heaven. Was this their doing?”

[P75]
“Yeah. It looks that way.”

[P76]
“There’s no one here.”

[P77]
I corrected myself at the speed of light.

[P78]
“It appears so, sir.”

[P79]
“So you are not certain yet.”

[P80]
“There is always some possibility of error. But although we haven’t found the formation, I’m convinced Dark Heaven was responsible.”

[P81]
“Dark Heaven. Dark Heaven…”

[P82]
Mungyeong murmured the words, then raised his head.

[P83]
He silently gazed at the dark night sky, where even the full moon had hidden itself. After a moment, he abruptly asked, “Did you notice anything strange about the corpses?”

[P84]
“Something strange?”

[P85]
“The wounds left on them.”

[P86]
Every death left traces. This was especially true of deaths caused by battles between martial artists.

[P87]
I had heard that a widely experienced master with a deep understanding of various martial arts could identify the weapon used—and even determine which form had killed the victim—simply by examining the wounds on a corpse.

[P88]
And the young medical apprentice before me possessed both the discernment and martial prowess to make him one of the finest examiners of the dead in Murim.

[P89]
“I have never seen wounds like these before. They seem to follow the principles of the very basic Three Calamities Sword Technique, yet they undulate like waves. They are exceedingly strange.”

[P90]
Mungyeong slowly raised one hand and swept it through the air. Thread-thin strands of internal energy flowed from it, glowing faintly in the darkness.

[P91]
“If I had to guess, the culprit did not use an ordinary weapon. It was an unusual weapon with a winding blade, something akin to a Snake Sword.”

[P92]
“I thought they’d been cut with Force.”

[P93]
“Your guess is correct. It was Force—or something every bit as sharp.”

[P94]
The only thing as sharp as Force was Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron.

[P95]
And no matter how thoroughly Dark Heaven had prepared, there was no way so many of its forces could have been armed with weapons made of Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron.

[P96]
*No matter how much gold you have, Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron is difficult to obtain.*

[P97]
This was not a question of capital. It was a question of resource scarcity.

[P98]
As I stood lost in thought, Mungyeong asked, “Did you examine all the corpses?”

[P99]
“Not all of them. I looked at the ones that stood out. I’m not particularly knowledgeable, so even after examining them myself, I couldn’t tell which martial arts or forms had been used.”

[P100]
“One of the corpses you examined belonged to Hwang Chung, the Yangtze One Saber. What did you make of it?”

[P101]
“He’d been cut cleanly in two at the waist by Force. But the decay was so severe that I couldn’t determine anything beyond that…”

[P102]
“And the Mad Water Saber Demon and the Wave Fox?”

[P103]
“Those two…”

[P104]
I suddenly frowned.

[P105]
A detail shared by all three corpses had just occurred to me.

[P106]
*…Only their upper bodies remained.*

[P107]
The lower halves of all three corpses were nowhere to be found.

[P108]
I had seen several other corpses like that, so it had not struck me as strange at the time. Now that I thought about it, though, it was certainly suspicious.

[P109]
“Didn’t the fish eat them?”

[P110]
“That would not be entirely wrong. From what I determined, the massacre at Donghu Stronghold took place ten days ago. The cold has been gone for some time, so severe decay is only natural. The corpses submerged in water would have fared even worse.”

[P111]
Warm sunlight and damp air had erased many of the traces left behind by death.

[P112]
But they had not erased everything.

[P113]
“By comparison, the commoners’ corpses still had their limbs relatively intact. Did you notice that?”

[P114]
“Yes. Those who hadn’t learned martial arts weren’t cut apart. They were crushed.”

[P115]
Unlike the river bandits’ corpses, the bodies of the children, women, and elderly had not been severed. Their entire bodies had simply been crushed and mangled.

[P116]
And there was one more thing.

[P117]
“The houses and the surrounding ground had caved in everywhere. That would have been impossible without a force of ten thousand geun, and it is not a method an internal-arts master with profound internal energy would choose.”

[P118]
“So, an external-arts master?”

[P119]
“There’s no one here, remember?”

[P120]
“…I was talking to myself.”

[P121]
He was awfully sensitive about this.

[P122]
After hurriedly making that excuse, I fell silent and considered the matter.

[P123]
Martial arts in Murim could broadly be divided into two categories.

[P124]
Internal arts emphasized the efficient use and application of internal energy. External arts also used internal energy, but focused on tempering the body to its absolute limits.

[P125]
Most people faced those two paths upon entering the world of martial arts, and most chose the former.

[P126]
Partly because training in external arts was excruciating, but also because achieving any meaningful results required long years of grueling perseverance.

[P127]
*Which means there are only a handful of Supreme Peak external-arts masters capable of this level of destruction.*

[P128]
There were hardly any Supreme Peak masters in the world to begin with, even if you turned the whole realm upside down and shook it out.

[P129]
I glanced at Mungyeong, silently asking for an answer. A faint crease appeared on the young medical apprentice’s smooth forehead.

[P130]
“Looking at me will do you no good. I do not know his identity either. No—I should say their identities, not his.”

[P131]
“There are two?”

[P132]
“At least two. Three at most.”

[P133]
“Three Supreme Peak masters…”

[P134]
“I would estimate that they are at least as formidable as the Qilian Three Fiends we faced in Sichuan. And at least one of them uses an unusual weapon.”

[P135]
*Fuck. What was this, some five-star rating? Why the hell were there three Supreme Peak masters together?*

[P136]
It was only because Mungyeong and Jeok Cheongang were holding down the fort that I could afford to leave at all. Without them here, I would have been too worried about what might happen to go anywhere.

[P137]
“With this much information, the Third Fiend might know something. He must have at least heard who his comrades were.”

[P138]
The Third Fiend we had captured in Sichuan was one of the reasons I was going to the Zhuge Clan.

[P139]
I had heard that he had become like a bipolar patient after his balls were crushed, but if I worked him over with enough care and dedication, he would not last long.

[P140]
*Maybe we can even put him out front and have him lead us to the formation.*

[P141]
That hopeful thought had barely crossed my mind when Mungyeong spoke.

[P142]
“Perhaps it is someone everyone already knows.”

[P143]
“What?”

[P144]
“I mean the one who uses that unusual weapon.”

[P145]
It took me quite a while to grasp what he meant.

[P146]
The realization struck like a hammer to the back of my head.

[P147]
I stared blankly at Mungyeong.

[P148]
“Are you serious?”

[P149]
“A seasoned Supreme Peak master. Forms and wounds so unusual that they are difficult to read. There cannot be many people at that realm who wield such a weapon.”

[P150]
“Then it really is…”

[P151]
A dry voice emerged from between Mungyeong’s lips.

[P152]
“The Dongting Fisherman. For now, he is the most likely suspect.”

[P153]
“…!”

[P154]
The eccentric master who had never left the area around Dongting Lake in his entire life.

[P155]
A Supreme Peak master who, unusually, used a fishing rod made of black wood as his signature weapon. Enraged by the tragic news concerning his friend, the head of the Sea Serpent Society, he had crossed Tianling Falls and disappeared.

[P156]
*Everything fits perfectly.*

[P157]
I had forgotten about him for a moment.

[P158]
This was no baseless suspicion.

[P159]
Unlike the others, the Dongting Fisherman’s corpse had never been found. The only trace he had left behind was his broken black-wood fishing rod.

[P160]
It was only a guess, but what if the Dongting Fisherman really was a member of Dark Heaven?

[P161]
“But the Dongting Fisherman Great Hero Zhuge told me about had no reason to do anything like this…”

[P162]
“Everything has a reason. The Dongting Fisherman is only human. He must have had a shadow he showed no one. Zhuge Feng is likely suspicious of him by now as well.”

[P163]
Mungyeong turned away, his voice cold.

[P164]
“Question everything, and remain vigilant. May martial fortune be with you.”
